solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird hard to be caught by countryman

indicators.note: to be caught by something is to end up held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a peasant is a man who works the land in the country
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough game bird gets trapped by a rural man out hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed game bird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Pleasure seeker acts with child

parts.note: to play is to act a part on stage
a boy is a male child

explanation.surface: A hedonist behaves like a kid.
explanation.definitionFit: A playboy is a wealthy man devoted to pleasure and leisure, a pleasure seeker.

clue.text: I engaged in turning over underwhelming content of inbox

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so the letter goes inside
turning over means flipping, so the built word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: lame means feeble or unimpressive, underwhelming

explanation.surface: Someone browses a dull inbox, flicking through its unexciting contents.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes in LAME after the L, giving LIAME, which 'turning over' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic messages are what an inbox holds, so the inbox's content is mail sent electronically.

clue.text: Get cast excited about airmen in theatrical skill

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go around the airmen
excited means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is made up of airmen

explanation.surface: A director tells the actors to be enthusiastic about pilots in a play about flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' makes STAGECT from GET CAST; 'about' puts it round RAF, between C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagecraft is skill and experience in writing or staging plays, the craft of the theatre.

clue.text: Spot water that's still liquid?

definitions.meaning: to spot is to see or catch sight of something
water that has not frozen is ..., read as two words

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer sees water and asks if it hasn't frozen yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer split as NOT ICE, water that is still a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to spot or observe it.

clue.text: Water vapour avoiding a plant's stalk

indicators.note: avoiding the letter means it is kept out, so it is taken away from the word

parts.note: steam is water in vapour form

explanation.surface: Something steers clear of vapour, reading as a note on how a plant's stalk keeps dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The main stalk of a plant, from which leaves and flowers grow, is called its stem.

clue.text: Struggle, having swallowed cocktail of rum in confusion

indicators.note: having swallowed means taken inside, so the mixed letters go within the struggle word

parts.note: toil is hard struggle or labour

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drinker struggles in a muddle after downing a rum cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance or uncertainty, a synonym of confusion.

clue.text: Strength from male ousting female in contest

indicators.note: ousting means pushing out and taking the place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a fight is a contest, as in a boxing match

explanation.surface: A man beats a woman in a test of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: M replaces the F of FIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Might means great power or strength, as in might is right.

clue.text: A skill in intricate fabric is offering a lot of options

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, sitting within the fabric word

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric with an intricate open pattern
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A craft displayed in a fine fabric offers a wide range of choices, like a varied shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu priced item by item gives diners many choices rather than a set meal, which is the phrase's restaurant sense.

clue.text: Lump of rock caught piece of cloth

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A lump of rock snagged a scrap of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A crag is a steep rugged mass of rock jutting out, a rocky outcrop.

clue.text: Very powerful potion men concocted by end of experiment

indicators.note: concocted means mixed up from ingredients, so these letters are blended into a new order
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Scientists brew a potent potion at the end of a lab experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipotent means all-powerful, having unlimited power, so very powerful indeed.

clue.text: Bitterness about head of Government is rubbish

indicators.note: about means around, so the bitterness word wraps round the other letter

parts.note: bile is bitterness or anger, from the bitter fluid of the liver

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cynic grumbles that resentment of the head of government is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge, the dirty water in a ship's hull, is slang for nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Male in favour of lying in bed for ease

indicators.note: lying in a bed puts these pieces inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
for means in favour of, as in voting for

explanation.surface: A man who likes staying in bed does so for his own ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort and ease are synonyms: both mean a state of physical relaxation free of strain.

clue.text: Solver's time to swallow good dairy product

indicators.note: to swallow is to take in, so the other letter goes inside

parts.note: the clue addresses the solver as you, so belonging to the solver is your

explanation.surface: It is the solver's turn to eat something good from the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes in YOURT after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: This fermented milk food is a typical product of the dairy, like cheese or butter.

clue.text: E.g. sock, squirming, may contain last of three lizards

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the shuffled letters wrap the extra letter
squirming means wriggling, so these letters are wriggled into a new order
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A sock wriggles about, perhaps because three lizards are hiding inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squirming' makes GECKOS from E.G. SOCK; 'may contain' puts it round E, the last letter of 'three', before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos are small nocturnal lizards that climb with sticky toe pads, so they are examples of lizards.

clue.text: Steering device? Twice left in a row

indicators.note: the doubled letters are placed in the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as in tiers of seats

indicators.note: twice means the letter is used two times over

explanation.surface: A sailor turns left twice in a row, wondering which device does the steering.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the lever used to turn a boat's rudder, a steering device.

clue.text: Curl of hair in item of jewellery permitted

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery worn on a finger
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A lock of hair is allowed to be worn with a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral curl of hair.

clue.text: First of six top people? A very funny person

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the cream are the best people, as in the cream of society

explanation.surface: A comic asks whether the first six people at the top are a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a scream is informal for saying they are hilarious, very amusing company.

clue.text: Calm current provided in photo

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed in the photo word

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
AC is alternating current
if means provided, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A still photograph shows a calm stream, if only in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means peaceful or calm in temper, which is why the ocean was given the name.

clue.text: I doze, sitting up with cold fear

indicators.note: sitting up in a down clue means the letters rise, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nap is a short doze

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off jolts upright, cold with fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear or alarm.

clue.text: Quantity of water upset canoe

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A capsized canoe leaves its paddler in a large body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, so it is a quantity of water, wryly understated.

clue.text: A king arriving in fenland city ahead of time

indicators.note: arriving in means entering, so these letters go inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in the Fens of Cambridgeshire
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch turns up in a Fens city before he is due.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in the Fens, the flat marshland of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means before the expected or appointed time.

clue.text: No agreement in a tight corner?

parts.note: OK is a word of agreement, as in saying yes

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a difficult situation finds no agreement there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tight corner' usually means a predicament; here it is literal, a small cramped corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or corner, the question mark flagging the literal reading of a tight spot.

clue.text: British tucking into breakfast food of an intellectual cast

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so this piece is placed within the food word

parts.note: cereal is a classic breakfast food, such as cornflakes

explanation.surface: A Briton digs into a bowl of cornflakes, apparently with a thoughtful air.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral describes someone more given to thought and reason than feeling, intellectual in character.

clue.text: Conservative remains ready

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Tory leftover is still prepared for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is the noun here, as in ready money or the readies, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money, or readies, is money in hand, the notes and coins of hard currency.

clue.text: Stone? Hate my rocks with stone

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so these letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Someone protests at being pelted with rocks and stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz prized as a gem, so it is a precious stone.
